questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Explain the following: why are halogens ortho-para directors even though they deactivate the ring?

answer.exemplar: Halogens withdraw electrons inductively through the sigma bond, which deactivates the ring toward electrophilic attack, but they donate a lone pair by resonance into the ring, and that resonance donation selectively stabilizes the sigma complexes for ortho and para attack; the resonance effect controls orientation while induction controls overall rate.

questions.explanation: Induction deactivates, resonance directs. Halogens withdraw electrons inductively through the sigma bond, which deactivates the ring toward electrophilic attack, but they donate a lone pair by resonance into the ring, and that resonance donation selectively stabilizes the sigma complexes for ortho and para attack; the resonance effect controls orientation while induction controls overall rate.
questions.hint: Different effects govern rate and orientation.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Explain the following: why do electron-withdrawing groups direct electrophiles to the meta position?

answer.exemplar: Ortho and para attack generate resonance contributors of the sigma complex that place positive charge on the ring carbon directly bonded to the electron-withdrawing group, which is highly destabilized; meta attack avoids that particularly unfavorable contributor, so meta substitution is favored.

questions.explanation: Ortho and para put cation next to the withdrawing group. Ortho and para attack generate resonance contributors of the sigma complex that place positive charge on the ring carbon directly bonded to the electron-withdrawing group, which is highly destabilized; meta attack avoids that particularly unfavorable contributor, so meta substitution is favored.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Explain the following: why is Friedel-Crafts acylation often preferred over alkylation for synthesis?

answer.exemplar: Acylation gives a deactivating ketone product that prevents further substitution, avoiding polyalkylation, and the acylium ion does not rearrange the way alkyl carbocations do, so a single clean product is obtained; the ketone can later be reduced if an alkyl group is desired.

questions.explanation: No rearrangement and no polyalkylation. Acylation gives a deactivating ketone product that prevents further substitution, avoiding polyalkylation, and the acylium ion does not rearrange the way alkyl carbocations do, so a single clean product is obtained; the ketone can later be reduced if an alkyl group is desired.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Explain the following: why are aryl diazonium salts such versatile synthetic intermediates?
